elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with face symptoms and any of:
elements.text: New sudden asymmetric weakness or numbness of face (with no/minimal forehead involvement), arm or leg; difficulty speaking or visual disturbance: consider stroke or TIA 152.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with face symptoms and any of:
elements.text: Sudden face/tongue swelling and any of: difficulty breathing, BP < 90/60, dizziness/collapse, abdominal pain, vomiting or exposure to possible allergen1, check for anaphylaxis 28.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with face symptoms and any of:
elements.text: Painful red facial swelling and temperature ≥ 38°C: facial cellulitis likely

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with face symptoms and any of:
elements.text: New swelling of face and blood/protein in urine: kidney disease likely
Manage and refer urgently:
If likely facial cellulitis with whole eyelid swollen, red and painful, orbital cellulitis likely. If delay in transfer, discuss with doctor.
If kidney disease likely and pulse > 100 or respiratory rate > 30, give face mask oxygen and furosemide 80mg slow IV, avoid IV fluids. If BP > 150/100, give amlodipine 5mg and furosemide 40mg orally.
FACE SYMPTOMS

1Common allergens include medication, food or insect bite/sting within the past few hours. 2Avoid if on RR-TB treatment. 3Common triggers include foods (milk, eggs, nuts, wheat, seafood), medications, insect bites/stings and latex.
Approach to patient with face symptoms not needing urgent attention • If rash on face 82. • If gum or tooth problem 54. • Manage according to face symptom/s:
Sudden progressive weakness of one side of face and unable
to wrinkle forehead or close eye. May have impaired taste
or dry eye.
Swelling of face
Bell’s palsy likely • Give prednisone as soon as possible (within 48 hours of onset): give 60mg daily for 7 days. If no better after 10 days, refer. • Protect eye: - Advise patient not to rub
eye - Keep eye moist with drops - Cover eye with transparent

eye shield during the day - Tape eyelid closed at night • Refer to physiotherapy, if available. • Refer same day if: otitis media, change in hearing, recent head injury, damage to cornea, unsure of diagnosis.
Painful swelling of one/both sides of face
with fever, headache,
body pain.

Mumps likely • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Advise patient can return to work after 5 days and symptoms usually resolve within 2 weeks. • Refer if: - Neck stiffness - Painful scrotal
swelling - Loss of hearing - Abdominal pain.
Painless swelling of lips/eyes

Angioedema likely • If airway obstruction (snoring, gurgling, noisy breathing), assess airway 16 and manage for anaphylaxis 28. • If no airway obstruction: if urticaria or itch present, give cetirizine 10mg or promethazine 25-50mg IM. • If on enalapril: stop enalapril, never restart and educate patient to avoid it in future. Doctor to review medication. • Help to identify and advise to avoid triggers3. • Monitor until swelling resolves. • If swelling not resolving or no obvious cause, refer same day. • Record in patient’s notes. • Advise to return urgently if difficulty breathing or symptoms worsen.
Face pain
Pain on one side of face Pain when pushing on forehead/cheeks, headache
worse on bending forward. Thick nasal/postnasal
discharge, recent common cold.

Sinusitis likely • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Give sodium chloride 0.9% nose drops as needed. • Give oxymetazoline 0.05% 2 drops in each nostril 8 hourly as needed for a maximum of 5 days. Advise against overuse which may worsen blocked nose. • If symptoms ≥ 10 days, temperature ≥ 38°C, purulent nasal discharge, face pain ≥ 3 days, or symptoms worsen after initial improvement of common cold, give amoxicillin 500mg 8 hourly for 5 days. If severe penicillin allergy (history of anaphylaxis, urticaria or angioedema) give instead azithromycin 500mg daily for 3 days. • If recurrent, test for HIV 124. • If poor response to antibiotic, refer. • Refer same day if: - Tooth infection - Swelling over sinus or around eye - Neck stiffness.
Recurrent
intense, superficial, stabbing pain
Trigeminal neuralgia likely • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed. • If needed, add tramadol 50mg 6 hourly. • Refer.
Previous shingles
on same side of
face

Post-herpetic neuralgia likely • Give amitriptyline2 25mg (10mg if ≥ 65 years) at night. If no response, increase by 25mg every 2 weeks, up to 75mg at night. • If pain ≥ 3 months, assess and advise 76. • If poor response, refer.
